ai.description: The Chequered Keelback is a medium-sized snake (up to 1.2m) with a yellow-to-olive body featuring a black, checkerboard pattern. It is distinguished by two black streaks below each eye.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable cue for *Fowlea piscator* is the pair of distinct, black, V-shaped "tear-drop" marks beneath each eye, which are absent in similar-looking water snakes.
ai.habitat: The Chequered Keelback inhabits freshwater bodies like ponds, lakes, and marshes across the Indian subcontinent, ranging from sea level up to 2,000 meters in elevation.
ai.behavior: The Chequered Keelback is primarily diurnal and an active hunter, often diving underwater to forage for fish and frogs in wetlands, ponds, and rice paddies.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Chequered Keelback is oviparous, breeding primarily during the monsoon season (June–September). Females lay a single clutch of 15–80 eggs in underground burrows.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Chequered Keelback is widespread across the Indian subcontinent, occurring from the plains up to 2,000m in diverse wetlands, marshes, and agricultural landscapes.
